nfl-2007-11-25-sf-ari: An eight-game losing streak ended in one of the wildest finishes of the 2007 NFL season as San Francisco beat Arizona 37–31 in overtime. [[espn:8479|Frank Gore]] powered the 49ers with 116 rushing yards and two touchdowns on 21 carries, plus 11 receptions for 98 yards. Across the field, [[espn:1682|Kurt Warner]] threw for 484 yards and two touchdowns, both to [[espn:5528|Larry Fitzgerald]], who caught nine passes for 156 yards.

The lead changed repeatedly. [[espn:649|Trent Dilfer]] connected with [[espn:4655|Arnaz Battle]] for a 57-yard third-quarter touchdown, but Arizona reclaimed the advantage in the fourth. Gore broke free for a 35-yard touchdown with 1:15 remaining to put San Francisco up 31–28. Warner marched Arizona downfield in the closing seconds, and [[espn:2300|Neil Rackers]] kicked a 19-yard field goal as regulation expired to force overtime.

Arizona nearly won it after Warner found [[espn:1994|Sean Morey]] for 62 yards, but a delay-of-game penalty preceded Rackers' missed 32-yard field-goal attempt. A punt and penalty later backed the Cardinals up to their own three. [[espn:8551|Ronald Fields]] sacked Warner in the end zone and forced a fumble that [[espn:4697|Tully Banta-Cain]] recovered for the walk-off touchdown. San Francisco swept its season series against Arizona and finally broke through after eight straight losses.
